{

      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go",
      "line": 137,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Fine-grained BuildIndex lock permits concurrent builds for the same key",
      "body": "BuildIndex now takes cacheMu only when inserting into b.cache. getOrCreateIndex in resource/search.go is not singleflight: callers can both call GetIndex, see nil, and call build concurrently. For file-backed indexes both goroutines call bleve.New on the same directory at the same time, which can fail or corrupt the index; even for memory indexes, the later insertion can overwrite a fresher index. Re-check the cache after acquiring cacheMu or add per-key singleflight before building."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 190,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Ignored build resource version causes permanent index gaps",
      "body": "s.build returns the last RV consumed from ListIterator, and the call in init discards it. After all builds, init starts WatchWriteEvents, but the SQL implementation starts from the latest RV at that moment and has no since parameter. Writes that land after a resource's ListIterator scan and before WatchWriteEvents starts are neither in the built index nor replayed, so the index can remain stale at least until restart or reindex."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 189,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Data race in init errgroup goroutines",
      "body": "The goroutines launched by group.Go all execute totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) using variables captured from the enclosing function. These are unsynchronized concurrent writes to the same variables (and err is returned), so this is a data race: increments can be lost and error propagation is undefined. Use local variables in the closure and an atomic counter, or update metrics after group.Wait."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go",
      "line": 208,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Watch goroutine panics on closed channel",
      "body": "The search watcher loop reads v := <-events without checking ok or selecting on a done context. When the backend closes the event stream during shutdown, v is a nil *WrittenEvent and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type, causing an unrecovered panic. It also uses context.Background() rather than a cancelable context, so it cannot be stopped cleanly. Check the ok value and return on channel close, and use a cancellable context."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go",
      "line": 258,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Error path leaks the server context and started services",
      "body": "NewResourceServer creates a cancelable ctx for the server's background work and then calls s.Init(ctx). If Init fails, it returns nil, err without calling s.cancel() or stopping the lifecycle. Since the server is not returned, the caller cannot call Stop. By that point search.init may already have started its watch goroutine, and Init may have initialized the backend, so these resources leak. Cancel ctx and perform cleanup on this path."
    },

    }

findings.title: Fine-grained BuildIndex lock permits concurrent builds for the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex now takes cacheMu only when inserting into b.cache. getOrCreateIndex in resource/search.go is not singleflight: callers can both call GetIndex, see nil, and call build concurrently. For file-backed indexes both goroutines call bleve.New on the same directory at the same time, which can fail or corrupt the index; even for memory indexes, the later insertion can overwrite a fresher index. Re-check the cache after acquiring cacheMu or add per-key singleflight before building.

findings.title: Ignored build resource version causes permanent index gaps
findings.body: s.build returns the last RV consumed from ListIterator, and the call in init discards it. After all builds, init starts WatchWriteEvents, but the SQL implementation starts from the latest RV at that moment and has no since parameter. Writes that land after a resource's ListIterator scan and before WatchWriteEvents starts are neither in the built index nor replayed, so the index can remain stale at least until restart or reindex.

findings.title: Data race in init errgroup goroutines
findings.body: The goroutines launched by group.Go all execute totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) using variables captured from the enclosing function. These are unsynchronized concurrent writes to the same variables (and err is returned), so this is a data race: increments can be lost and error propagation is undefined. Use local variables in the closure and an atomic counter, or update metrics after group.Wait.

findings.title: Watch goroutine panics on closed channel
findings.body: The search watcher loop reads v := <-events without checking ok or selecting on a done context. When the backend closes the event stream during shutdown, v is a nil *WrittenEvent and handleEvent immediately dereferences evt.Type, causing an unrecovered panic. It also uses context.Background() rather than a cancelable context, so it cannot be stopped cleanly. Check the ok value and return on channel close, and use a cancellable context.

findings.title: Error path leaks the server context and started services
findings.body: NewResourceServer creates a cancelable ctx for the server's background work and then calls s.Init(ctx). If Init fails, it returns nil, err without calling s.cancel() or stopping the lifecycle. Since the server is not returned, the caller cannot call Stop. By that point search.init may already have started its watch goroutine, and Init may have initialized the backend, so these resources leak. Cancel ctx and perform cleanup on this path.

findings.title: Postgres integration test skipped
findings.body: This change disables the storage-server integration test for postgres due to CI failures. That leaves the postgres unified-storage path without this integration coverage and may hide regressions in the new eager-init behavior. Either fix the underlying failure or file and track a concrete issue rather than silently skipping.
